correctness.rationale: On a compact stationary family of complete trajectories, delayed and current one-time marginals agree. Stationarity of the current coordinate and of its square gives the two exact balances. Their difference from products of means gives the covariance identity. Size-biasing converts the first balance to an exact exponential moment; strict Jensen then gives the equilibrium moment floor, with equality forcing a constant complete trajectory and hence the positive equilibrium. The variance lower bound is an immediate Cauchy–Schwarz consequence. The packaged checker independently verifies the algebraic implications.

A complete open 2016 same-equation treatment likewise surveys the classical qualitative theory but contains no located average/moment/mean formulation. Direct semantic searches for invariant-measure moments and stationary mean balances returned no same-object result stating the accepted size-biased floor or delayed-recruitment covariance.

value.rationale: Adult population and delayed recruitment are the two defining observables in Nicholson's canonical delay mechanism. The exact covariance law quantifies how present abundance co-varies with the delayed nonlinear birth input in every compact stationary regime, independent of whether that regime is periodic or more complicated. The size-biased moment floor gives a parameter-exact amplitude constraint tied to the biologically meaningful positive equilibrium and is strict for every non-equilibrium stationary state. These provide direct consistency checks for simulated or empirical stationary Nicholson cycles beyond qualitative oscillation or stability.
